beats.phrase: What does this little 's' actually stand for?
Say you post a cat picture.
That 's' keeps it safe while it travels from your phone to the website.
Because on the way, it hops through Wi-Fi, routers and cables you don't own.
So before it leaves your phone, your browser locks it.
Anyone snooping can see where it's going, but not what's inside.
That lock is called TLS.
So who unlocks it at the other end?
A big website isn't one computer.
Everything you send hits a front server first.
That front server holds the website's key, so it unlocks your picture and hands it to the computers behind it.
That's normal. It's part of the website.
So the lock ends right there, at the front server.
That's why it's called TLS termination.
Why unlock it at the front?
Unlocking takes work, so the front server does it for everyone, and the computers behind it don't have to.
The catch? Past the front server, your picture can travel on unlocked, inside the website.
Some websites lock it again in there. Some don't.
So that little 's'? It stands for secure.
It locks your picture from your phone to the website's front server.
After that, it's up to the website.
Send this to someone who trusts that little 's'.
